deepdive.sec: FMCG / Ayurvedic Personal Care & Natural Foods

bull_bear.body: Prioritizing reinvestment of cost savings into consumer communication (A&P) to drive volume; balancing margin expansion with market share gains.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Weather dependency for Beverage/Glucose segments; Regulatory surprises (e.g., labor codes); Competitive intensity in modern trade (Oral Care); Geopolitical/tariff impacts on exports.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Optimistic on sequential demand recovery; cautious on weather-dependent categories; confident in margin restoration to 20% levels; transparent about one-offs and inventory corrections.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Chyawanprash primary sales were flat due to deliberate avoidance of pre-season loading to clear legacy trade inventory, masking strong 11% tertiary offtake; Hair Oil growth is largely value-driven (price) due to prior coconut oil inflation, whereas Oral Care is increasingly volume-driven; 2% price hike deferred due to anti-profiteering norms will roll over in Q4/FY27.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Supported by Strong Balance Sheet": Net Cash of INR 84 Bn as on 31st March 26 and Net Worth of INR 118 Bn.
- Return on Invested Capital of 42% in FY26.
- Dividend paid of INR 14.6 Bn in FY26 with a stated Dividend Payout Ratio of 77%.
- FY26 profitability: Consolidated Revenue INR 13,193 Cr, Operating Profit INR 2,452 Cr (18.6% operating profit margin) and PAT INR 1,895 Cr (14.4% PAT margin), described as "Quality Growth across all levers".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: HPC +10.6% (Hair Oil +19.1%, Shampoo +6.2%); Oral Care +10% (Meswak/Herbal +25%); Home Care (Odonil double-digit); Healthcare (Honey +10%, Chyawanprash flat primary but +11% offtake); Digestives +7%; Beverages (Real Activ +38%, Coconut Water +52%); International +11% INR (+7.5% CC).

business.body:

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as "AMONG TOP 4 FMCG COMPANIES IN INDIA" and "A Leader in Ayurveda and Natural Healthcare", with 8 out of 10 households consuming Dabur products.
- Claims #1 player positions in Juices & Nectars, Chyawanprash, Honey, MRC, Bleaches and Hair Oils (footnoted: in Value Added Hair Oils), and #2 player positions in Oral care, Glucose and Air Fresheners.
- "STRONG OVERSEAS PRESENCE WITH 27% SALIENCY"; the deck asserts market leadership in international hair care and toothpaste across Saudi Arabia, Egypt and the UAE.
- Business structure is DOMESTIC (73%) - split Home & Personal Care (51%), Healthcare (28%), Food & Beverages (21%) - and International (27%).
- Twenty-year track record cited as Revenue from Operations 20-Year CAGR of 10% (INR 1,900 Cr in FY2006 to INR 13,193 Cr in FY2026), PAT 20-Year CAGR of 11.5% (INR 214 Cr to INR 1,895 Cr) and Market Capitalization up 10x in the last 20 years (INR 7,109 Cr to INR 72,801 Cr).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Market share] The deck claims 90% of the portfolio gained market shares in FY26.
- [International] International Business grew by 6.2% in constant-currency terms in FY26; the FY26 international revenue breakdown is Middle East 27%, Africa 23%, Asia 19%, Europe 16% and Americas 15%.
- [AI] DaburGPT is presented as an internal AI tool "Empowering Smarter Decisions Across Functions" - enhancing productivity through AI-enabled insights, automation and collaboration, and supporting faster decision-making, with AI leveraged across the Dabur value chain.
- [Route to market] Local-event marketing (melas, festivals, Durga Puja, Ramleela, trade fairs and elections) plus print media and wall painting remain explicit visibility levers alongside digital.
- [Deck context] This is the presentation made to shareholders at the 51st Annual General Meeting held on August 06, 2026, delivered by Mohit Malhotra, CEO - it is an AGM deck, not a standard quarterly results deck.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Input costs (Coconut oil, SLES, Vegetable oils) softening after spikes; Q3 PAT impacted by one-time labor law provision; FY27 margin expansion planned via passing on 20-25% of gross margin upside to operating profit while reinvesting rest in A&P; 2% price increase planned for Q4 carry-forward.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: High single-digit for Q4FY26; High single-to-low double-digit for FY27; Margin: Sequential improvement expected; FY27 target to return to ~20% operating margin; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: Reinvestment of gross margin upside into advertising (75-80%) and margin expansion (20-25%).

deepdive.thesis: Dabur India reported 6.1% consolidated revenue growth in Q3FY26, driven by a post-GST transition demand recovery and strong rural performance, with operating profit expanding 7.7% despite a one-time labor law provision. Management guides for high single-digit growth in Q4 and a return to ~20% operating margins in FY27 as input costs soften and deferred price hikes roll over.

open.item: The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 5.50 per equity share for FY 2025-26, taking the aggregate dividend for the year to Rs 8.25 per equity share, in accordance with the Dividend Distribution Policy.

The new greenfield factory at Tindivanam, Tamil Nadu is expected to begin operations by end of FY 2026-27 with Red Toothpaste and Gulabari, with more lines and product categories to be added in the future.
Build the new manufacturing facility at Tindivanam, Tamil Nadu, whose construction began during the year, to add future-ready domestic capacity.
The Tindivanam, Tamil Nadu greenfield factory is expected to begin operations by end of FY 2026-27 with Red Toothpaste and Gulabari, with more lines and product categories to be added in the future.
Dabur Ventures, a Rs 500 crore investment platform, will invest in high-potential, new-age digital-first brands aligned with Dabur's long-term strategic priorities.
The Company remains committed to premiumisation in Dabur Honey and plans to introduce additional premium variants going forward, building on Organic and Sundarbans Honey.
Reinvent the Go-to-Market model with GTM 2.0 through Project Saksham as a stated forward priority.
Drive disciplined cost optimisation through Project Samriddhi.
Explore strategic M&A opportunities for portfolio diversification and acceleration.
Set up a Digital Marketing Global Capability Centre to complement the already operational IT GCC, using advanced MarTech, AI-led insights and data-driven execution.
Dabur Egypt is creating capacity for Hobby Body Wash and Herbolene after enhancing oral care and shampoo capacity and operationalising phase 1 of the new greenfield plant at 10th of Ramadan City.

NewU will pursue strategic retail expansion on the FOCO (Franchise-Owned, Company-Operated) model and grow its exclusive private label portfolio, after adding 14 stores in FY 2025-26 to reach 105 stores.

The international hair care business will drive growth through innovation and focused geographic expansion, particularly across the Caribbean markets and Canada, with a sustained emphasis on e-commerce and 3PL-supported scale-up.

risks.note: The outbreak of war in early 2026 disrupted oil supply chains, drove up energy prices and triggered inflationary pressures worldwide; uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz and financial tightening slowed growth, and management flags global uncertainties and energy price volatility as key watchpoints for FMCG demand and input costs.
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and energy price volatility

risks.note: Unseasonal rains and erratic weather, particularly during peak summer months, tempered demand for seasonal categories; consumption in the healthcare portfolio and brands such as Dabur Glucose was explicitly impacted by unseasonal rains and a shorter summer.
risks.risk: Weather volatility and seasonality of key categories

risks.note: Urban demand, particularly in traditional trade, remained under pressure in the first half of the year and recovered only slowly, making a large part of the India FMCG business dependent on a gradual and uncertain urban recovery.
risks.risk: Soft urban demand in traditional trade

risks.note: The expansion of e-commerce and quick commerce is rapidly reshaping buying behaviour and channel salience, requiring continual re-engineering of route-to-market, assortment and trade economics to avoid losing share in a shifting retail landscape.
risks.risk: Channel disruption from e-commerce and quick commerce

risks.note: Dabur describes operating in a highly competitive market where consumer connect is the key differentiator; sustaining market share gains depends on continued brand investment, innovation and premiumisation.

Global inflation is expected to inch up significantly on the Middle East war situation; the Company relies on judicious price increases, premiumisation and cost management, which may lag if input inflation accelerates.

Dabur has manufacturing presence across nine countries and sells in more than 120, exposing the consolidated business to currency movement, geopolitical complexity in certain regions and trade or tariff policy shifts.
risks.risk: International business exposure across more than 120 countries

risks.note: Rural demand, which trended ahead of urban markets, was aided by favourable agricultural performance, an above-normal monsoon, government welfare initiatives and GST rationalisation - a reversal in any of these would directly affect Dabur's rural-weighted portfolio.
risks.risk: Dependence on rural demand and the agricultural cycle
